name: Dal Tadka
description: Soft yellow lentils finished with a sizzling tempering of cumin, garlic and chilli.
steps: Wash the dal until the water runs clear. Boil it with water, turmeric and salt in a pressure cooker for 4 whistles, or simmer covered for 30-35 minutes until completely soft.
Mash the cooked dal lightly with a spoon and keep it warm.
Heat oil in a pan. Add cumin seeds and let them sizzle for 10 seconds.
Add asafoetida, chopped garlic and slit green chilli. Fry until the garlic turns light golden.
Add chopped onion and cook for 4-5 minutes until golden. Add tomatoes and red chilli powder and cook until the tomatoes turn soft and the oil separates.
Pour this tempering into the dal, mix well and simmer for 5 minutes. Add hot water if too thick.
Garnish with coriander leaves and serve hot with rice or roti.
tips: Letting the cumin sizzle in hot oil releases its aroma. Do not let the garlic turn brown or it turns bitter.
A spoon of ghee at the end gives restaurant-style richness.
substitutions: Use masoor dal for a faster cook of about 15 minutes.
No asafoetida? Skip it; add a little extra garlic.

name: Aloo Matar
description: Potatoes and green peas simmered in a spiced onion-tomato gravy.
steps: Peel the potatoes and cut them into medium cubes. Puree the tomatoes.
Heat oil in a pan. Add cumin seeds and wait until they sizzle.
Add chopped onions and cook for 6-8 minutes until golden brown. Add ginger garlic paste and cook for 1 minute.
Add turmeric, coriander powder and chilli powder with a splash of water, then add the tomato puree. Cook for 6-7 minutes until the oil separates from the masala.
Add the potatoes, peas and salt. Stir to coat well for 2 minutes.
Add the water, cover and cook on medium-low for 15-18 minutes until the potatoes are tender.
Stir in garam masala, simmer 2 minutes and serve hot.
tips: Cook the masala until the oil leaves the sides. Raw masala tastes flat.
Mash 2-3 potato pieces into the gravy to thicken it naturally.
substitutions: Frozen peas work; add them for the last 8 minutes.
No ginger garlic paste? Use grated ginger plus 2 chopped garlic cloves.

name: Aloo Gobi
description: A dry sauteed curry of cauliflower and potato with turmeric, cumin and coriander.
steps: Cut the cauliflower into medium florets and the potatoes into 2 cm cubes. Soak the florets in warm salted water for 10 minutes, then drain well.
Heat oil in a wide pan and add cumin seeds. When they sizzle, add grated ginger and chopped onion.
Cook the onion for 5 minutes until golden, then add the chopped tomato and cook until soft and mushy.
Add turmeric, coriander powder, chilli powder and salt. Stir for 1 minute.
Add the potatoes first and cook covered for 5 minutes. Then add the cauliflower and mix well.
Cover and cook on low for 12-15 minutes, stirring gently now and then, until both are tender. Do not add water; the steam is enough.
Sprinkle garam masala and coriander leaves, toss and serve with roti.
tips: Use a wide pan and do not crowd it so the vegetables roast instead of steaming into mush.
Cut the potatoes slightly smaller than the cauliflower since they take longer.
substitutions: Add a pinch of amchur (dry mango powder) for tang if you have no tomato.

name: Palak Paneer
description: Soft paneer cubes in a smooth, lightly spiced spinach gravy.
steps: Blanch the spinach in boiling water for 2 minutes, then move it straight into cold water. This keeps it bright green. Blend with green chillies into a smooth puree.
Cut the paneer into cubes. Soak in warm water for 10 minutes to keep it soft.
Heat oil, add cumin seeds, then chopped onion. Cook until golden.
Add ginger garlic paste and chopped tomatoes with the chilli powder. Cook until soft and the oil separates.
Pour in the spinach puree and salt. Simmer on low for 5-7 minutes, stirring often.
Add the paneer and garam masala. Simmer 3 minutes. Stir in the cream and turn off the heat.
tips: Do not overcook the spinach after blending or it turns dull and bitter.
Pan-fry the paneer cubes lightly first for a richer taste.
substitutions: Replace cream with 2 tbsp of milk or cashew paste for a lighter gravy.
Use tofu cubes in place of paneer for a vegan version, and oil plus coconut milk in place of cream.

name: Chana Masala
description: Chickpeas simmered in a tangy, dark, robustly spiced onion-tomato masala.
steps: Soak the chickpeas overnight. Pressure cook with salt for 6-7 whistles until soft. For canned chickpeas, rinse and skip this step.
Heat oil, add cumin seeds and bay leaf. Add chopped onions and cook for 8 minutes until deep golden brown.
Add ginger garlic paste and cook for 1 minute.
Add pureed tomatoes, turmeric, coriander powder and chilli powder. Cook for 8-10 minutes until the oil separates.
Add the chickpeas with 2 cups of the cooking water. Mash a few chickpeas against the pan to thicken the gravy.
Add chana masala powder and simmer covered for 10-12 minutes. Finish with amchur powder and serve with bhature, rice or roti.
tips: Browning the onions well gives the dish its deep color and flavor.
Keep a little of the chickpea cooking water: it adds body to the gravy.
substitutions: No amchur? Use 1 tbsp lemon juice at the end.
No chana masala powder? Use garam masala plus a pinch of extra coriander powder.

name: Rajma Masala
description: Red kidney beans in a thick, mildly spiced tomato-onion gravy, a Punjabi comfort classic.
steps: Soak the rajma in plenty of water overnight, at least 8 hours. Drain and pressure cook with salt and fresh water for 8-10 whistles until very soft.
Heat oil, add cumin seeds, bay leaf and cinnamon. Add chopped onions and cook for 8-10 minutes until deep golden.
Add ginger garlic paste and cook 1 minute. Add pureed tomatoes, turmeric, coriander powder and chilli powder.
Cook the masala for 8-10 minutes until the oil separates from the sides.
Add the cooked rajma along with its liquid. Mash a few beans to thicken the gravy.
Simmer on low for 15-20 minutes. Stir in garam masala and serve hot with steamed rice.
tips: Never cook kidney beans that are not fully soft; undercooked rajma upsets the stomach.
Even tinned beans improve if simmered in the masala for 20 minutes.
substitutions: Use 2 cans of kidney beans, drained and rinsed, instead of soaking.

name: Bhindi Masala
description: Crisp-tender okra stir-fried with onion and a dry spice mix.
steps: Wash the okra and dry it completely with a clean cloth. Wet okra turns slimy. Trim the ends and cut into 2 cm pieces.
Heat 2 tbsp oil in a wide pan. Fry the okra on medium-high for 8-10 minutes until it is no longer sticky and has light brown edges. Remove and keep aside.
In the same pan add 1 tbsp oil and cumin seeds. When they sizzle, add sliced onion and cook until golden.
Add chopped tomato, turmeric, coriander powder, chilli powder and salt. Cook until the tomato softens.
Return the okra to the pan and mix gently. Cook uncovered for 4-5 minutes.
Finish with amchur powder and serve with roti.
tips: Dry okra and do not cover the pan once it is added. This keeps the pieces from turning slimy.
Add salt at the end to keep the okra crisp.
substitutions: Use lemon juice instead of amchur powder.

name: Jeera Rice
description: Fluffy basmati rice tempered with fragrant cumin seeds.
steps: Wash the rice in several changes of water until the water is almost clear. Soak for 20-30 minutes, then drain.
Heat oil in a pot. Add cumin seeds, bay leaf and cloves. Let them sizzle for 20 seconds.
Add the drained rice and gently fry for 1-2 minutes.
Add water and salt. Bring to a boil.
Cover tightly, reduce the heat to the lowest and cook for 12-14 minutes until the water is absorbed.
Turn off the heat and rest it covered for 5 minutes. Fluff with a fork.
tips: The water ratio is about 1.75 cups per cup of soaked basmati. Unsoaked rice needs slightly more.
Do not stir the rice while it cooks or it turns sticky.
substitutions: Add 1 tsp ghee on top at the end for extra aroma.

name: Vegetable Sambar
description: A tangy lentil and vegetable stew flavored with sambar powder and tamarind.
steps: Wash the dal and pressure cook with turmeric and 2 cups of water for 4-5 whistles until very soft. Mash it well.
Soak the tamarind in 0.5 cup of warm water for 10 minutes, then squeeze out the pulp and discard the fibres.
In a pot, boil the vegetables, onion and tomato with the remaining water and salt for 10-12 minutes until tender.
Add the tamarind pulp and sambar powder. Boil for 5 minutes until the raw smell goes.
Add the mashed dal and simmer for 8-10 minutes, adding water if too thick.
For the tempering, heat oil in a small pan. Add mustard seeds, and when they pop add dried chillies, curry leaves and asafoetida.
Pour the tempering over the sambar. Serve with idli, dosa or rice.
tips: Tamarind quantity decides the tang. Start with less and adjust.
Sambar tastes even better the next day.
substitutions: Use 1 tbsp of lemon juice if you have no tamarind, added at the very end.

name: Lemon Rice
description: Cooked rice tossed with turmeric, mustard seeds, curry leaves, peanuts and fresh lemon juice.
steps: Spread the cooked rice on a plate so it cools and the grains separate.
Heat oil in a pan. Add mustard seeds and wait for them to pop.
Add chana dal and peanuts. Fry on medium until golden and crunchy, about 2 minutes.
Add slit green chillies, curry leaves and asafoetida. Stir for 15 seconds.
Add turmeric and salt, then turn off the heat.
Add the rice and lemon juice. Toss gently so the grains do not break.
tips: Add the lemon juice after switching off the heat. Cooking it turns the flavor bitter.
Day-old rice works best.
substitutions: Use cashews if peanuts are not available or you want to avoid them.

name: Kanda Poha
description: Light flattened rice with onion, peanuts, turmeric and a squeeze of lemon, a classic Maharashtrian breakfast.
steps: Rinse the poha in a colander under running water for 20-30 seconds, until just soft. Do not soak it. Let it drain and sprinkle with salt and sugar.
Heat oil in a pan and fry the peanuts until golden. Remove and keep aside.
In the same oil add mustard seeds. When they pop, add curry leaves and green chillies.
Add diced potato and cook covered on low for 6-8 minutes until tender. Add chopped onion and cook for 3 minutes.
Add turmeric, then the drained poha. Mix gently and cook covered for 2-3 minutes.
Add lemon juice, peanuts and coriander leaves. Mix lightly and serve hot.
tips: Overwashed poha turns to paste. It should stay soft but separate.
The tiny amount of sugar balances the sourness.
substitutions: Skip the potato for a quicker version.

name: Rava Upma
description: Soft, savory semolina porridge tempered with mustard seeds, curry leaves and vegetables.
steps: Dry roast the rava in a pan on low heat for 4-5 minutes until it smells nutty. Keep aside.
Heat oil in the same pan. Add mustard seeds and urad dal and fry until the dal turns golden.
Add curry leaves, green chillies and grated ginger, then chopped onion and carrot. Cook for 3-4 minutes.
Add the water and salt. Bring to a rolling boil.
Lower the heat and add the rava in a slow stream, stirring constantly to avoid lumps.
Cover and cook for 2-3 minutes until it absorbs all the water. Serve hot with chutney or pickle.
tips: Pour the rava slowly while stirring. This is what prevents lumps.
Roasted rava keeps the upma from turning sticky.
substitutions: Use frozen mixed vegetables instead of fresh carrot.

name: Gujarati Kadhi
description: A smooth, lightly sweet and tangy yogurt and gram flour soup tempered with cumin and cloves.
steps: Whisk the yogurt, besan, water, sugar, salt and turmeric into a completely smooth batter with no lumps.
Pour it into a pot, add grated ginger and slit green chilli. Bring to a gentle boil on medium heat, stirring continuously.
Reduce the heat and simmer for 12-15 minutes, stirring often, until the raw besan smell disappears.
For the tempering, heat oil in a small pan. Add cumin, mustard seeds, cloves, dried red chilli and curry leaves.
Pour the tempering into the kadhi and mix. Serve hot with rice or khichdi.
tips: Stir continuously at first, otherwise the kadhi can split.
Use slightly sour yogurt for better flavor.
substitutions: Use thin coconut milk and lemon juice for a dairy-free version, though the taste is different.

name: Baingan Bharta
description: Smoky roasted brinjal mashed and cooked with onion, tomato and spices.
steps: Rub a little oil on the brinjal and prick it with a fork. Roast it directly over a gas flame, turning often, for 10-12 minutes until the skin is charred and the flesh is soft. In an oven, roast at 220 C for 35-40 minutes.
Let it cool, peel off the skin and mash the pulp roughly.
Heat oil, add cumin seeds, then chopped garlic and green chillies. Fry for 30 seconds.
Add chopped onion and cook for 6-7 minutes until golden. Add tomatoes and cook until soft.
Add turmeric, chilli powder, coriander powder and salt. Stir for 1 minute.
Add the mashed brinjal and cook for 8-10 minutes, stirring, until the oil separates.
Finish with garam masala and coriander leaves. Serve with roti or paratha.
tips: The smoky flavor comes from charring the skin well, so do not rush it.
Cool the brinjal slightly before peeling for easier handling.
substitutions: No open flame? Roast in the oven, then add a tiny drop of smoked paprika if you have it.

name: Paneer Bhurji
description: Crumbled paneer scrambled with onion, tomato and spices, a quick protein-rich dish.
steps: Crumble the paneer coarsely with your hands.
Heat oil and add cumin seeds. When they sizzle, add chopped green chilli and onion. Cook until the onion is soft and light golden.
Add ginger garlic paste and capsicum. Cook for 2 minutes.
Add tomato, turmeric, chilli powder and salt. Cook for 3-4 minutes until the tomato turns mushy.
Add the crumbled paneer and mix gently. Cook for 2-3 minutes only.
Sprinkle garam masala and coriander leaves. Serve with roti or toasted bread.
tips: Do not cook paneer for long. It turns rubbery.
A splash of milk at the end keeps it moist.
substitutions: Crumbled firm tofu works as a vegan alternative; add a pinch of extra salt.

name: Moong Dal Khichdi
description: Soft, porridge-like rice and yellow lentils lightly spiced, the ultimate comfort food.
steps: Wash the rice and dal together until the water runs clear. Soak for 15 minutes and drain.
Heat oil in a pressure cooker. Add cumin seeds, asafoetida, grated ginger and slit green chilli. Fry for 30 seconds.
Add the rice-dal mix, turmeric, black pepper and salt. Stir for 1 minute.
Add the water and pressure cook for 3-4 whistles until the khichdi is soft and mushy.
Let the pressure release naturally. Mix well and adjust consistency with hot water.
Serve hot with pickle or papad.
tips: Khichdi thickens as it cools. Add hot water when reheating.
Add vegetables like carrot, peas or beans for a fuller meal.
substitutions: Use a pot instead of a pressure cooker and simmer covered for 25-30 minutes, stirring now and then.
